findings.title: join() aborts terminating remaining flusher processes once the deadline is hit for one process
findings.body: In join(), the for-loop over self.processes.items() does `break` when the join deadline has passed for the *current* process index. Because break exits the entire for-loop (not just the inner while), any processes that come later in the dict are never waited on nor have .terminate() called on them. Previously there was only a single process and .terminate() was always reached after the wait loop; now, with multiple flusher processes, a timed-out shutdown can leave one or more real subprocesses running un-terminated after join() returns, leaking Kafka producer connections and Redis clients/orphaned processes.

findings.title: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard likely never true for spawn-context processes, so .kill() is silently skipped
findings.body: _ensure_processes_alive() now only calls process.kill() when isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is true. Processes here are created via self.mp_context.Process where self.mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context('spawn'); such a call returns an instance of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which is a sibling of (not a subclass of) the generic multiprocessing.context.Process class that multiprocessing.Process refers to. Consequently this isinstance check evaluates to False for real spawned subprocesses, meaning the unhealthy process is never killed before _create_process_for_shards spawns its replacement. Previously .kill() was called unconditionally (only ValueError was swallowed), so this is a regression: hung/unhealthy processes may now keep running alongside their replacements, consuming Redis connections and potentially double-producing flushed segments to Kafka.

findings.title: Memory usage may be double-counted across per-process shard buffers when computing backpressure threshold
findings.body: submit() now sums buffer.get_memory_info() across self.buffers.values(), where each buffer is a SpansBuffer scoped only to the shards owned by one flusher process. Previously a single SpansBuffer covering all assigned shards computed memory info once per distinct Redis node/cluster. If multiple shards (now split across different per-process buffers) map to the same underlying Redis node, that node's ServiceMemory will be reported and summed multiple times, inflating 'used'/'available' totals used to decide spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage backpressure. This can skew the used/available ratio and trigger (or fail to trigger) hard backpressure incorrectly depending on how shards are distributed across nodes and processes.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key between related timers ('shard' vs 'shards')
findings.body: The produce timer uses tags={"shard": shard_tag} while the wait_produce timer right below it uses tags={"shards": shard_tag} for the same shard_tag value. This inconsistency means the two related metrics (spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) cannot be correlated/filtered by the same tag key in dashboards or alerts, undermining the observability improvement this change is meant to add.

findings.title: Docstring overstates default flusher behavior
findings.body: The class docstring states SpanFlusher 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing,' but the actual process count is capped by max_processes (the --flusher-processes CLI option), whose default in src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py is 1. By default this still runs as a single flusher process handling all shards, identical to pre-PR behavior, unless operators explicitly raise --flusher-processes. The docstring should clarify that one-process-per-shard only happens when max_processes is unset/None or >= number of assigned shards.

findings.title: New multiprocess-flusher test only checks internal bookkeeping, not actual multi-process flush behavior
findings.body: test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts len(flusher.processes), max_processes, num_processes and the total shard count in process_to_shards_map; it never submits spans, advances the clock, and verifies that segments for shards handled by different processes are actually flushed/produced correctly, nor does it exercise the per-process restart path added in this PR. Given the PR's core change is spawning one process per shard group, there is no test exercising end-to-end correctness of flushing across multiple flusher processes.
